kinds.d: Chinese double-edged straight sword, made in bronze from the 7th century BCE and later in steel.

x.d: Bronze jian of King Goujian of Yue with a gold-inlaid bird-worm script inscription.
Bronze jian carried by officers of the Terracotta Army.
Rare two-handed jian.
Unsharpened semi-flexible stainless jian for tai chi solo forms.
Thin, highly flexible jian made for performance.

kinds.d: Single-edged Chinese sword for slashing and chopping, straight or curved; one of the four traditional weapons.

x.d: Willow-leaf sabre with a moderate curve; the commonest Chinese sabre and standard sidearm.
Goose-quill sabre, mostly straight with a curve near the tip, suited to thrusting.
Ox-tail sabre with a heavy blade flaring at the tip; a civilian weapon.
Falchion-like dao.
Long two-handed dao used against cavalry and pirates.
Deeply curved slashing sabre resembling a shamshir.
Straight single-handed belt sidearm, common in the Tang.
Long two-handed dao.
Short dao, generally shaped like a liuyedao.

kinds.d: Persian sword with a slim, radically curved blade, worn horizontally and used for slashing.

x.d: Slim curved blade tapering only near the tip, offset pommel, long quillons, bone, ivory or wood grip.
x.dt: wootz or plain steel · grip material

x.d: Hunting shamshir with an engraved blade, usually showing hunting scenes.
Afghan single-handed curved sword of the shamshir family.

kinds.d: Curved single-edged sabre of the Indian subcontinent with an all-metal disc-pommel hilt.

x.d: Mughal-era talwar: moderately curved blade, often widening towards the tip, on a disc hilt with knucklebow.
Talwar with a massive blade, often called an executioner's sword.
Talwar with an only slightly curved blade.
Straight-bladed talwar on a disc hilt.
Talwar with a yatagan-style forward-curved blade.
Talwar with a double-pointed blade.

kinds.d: Indian straight double-edged sword whose blade widens to a blunt tip, with a plate guard and spiked disc pommel.
One-handed curved Turkic and Ottoman sabre, often with a flared false edge (yelman) near the tip.

x.d: Distinct Ottoman sabre with yelman false edge.
Curved steppe cavalry sabre of Turkic peoples.
Late kilij with a short, broad, sharply curved blade.

kinds.d: Guardless Ottoman short sabre with a forward-curved single-edged blade and an eared pommel.

x.d: Yataghan with large bone or ivory pommel ears.
Yataghan with smaller horn or silver pommel ears.
T-hilted yataghan carried by Zeibeks of the Ionian coast.

kinds.d: Large single-edged Philippine sword whose blade widens towards the tip, often with a spikelet and carved pommel.
Single-edged, gently curved Southeast Asian sword with a round grip and little or no guard.

x.d: Dha with a straight or nearly straight spine.
Daab with a slightly curved spine.
Daab with a more pronounced curve and more carving.

kinds.d: Straight double-edged Sahel sword of about one metre, carried by the Tuareg, with a leather-covered hilt.
Ethiopian sword with a near-semicircular double-edged blade for hooking round a shield.

traditions.d: High-carbon crucible steel showing banded carbide patterns, traded west and behind Damascus steel blades.
traditions.tech: ore heated with carbon in sealed clay crucibles in a charcoal furnace
traditions.auth: Wave, ladder or rose banding from forging; modern smiths can now make visually identical patterns.

traditions.p: Spring and Autumn period (by tradition) to present
traditions.d: Sword craft traced to the smith Ou Yezi, on China's national intangible cultural heritage list since 2006.
traditions.auth: Judged by sharpness, cold glitter, blade density and fine metal carving.
